question: Should OpenClaw adopt this experiment-gated core Claws update-planning and capability-consent contract as the middle stage of the current diagnostics → plan → apply stack?
rationale: The PR adds a new public experimental CLI and versioned consent model across configuration, workspace, package, MCP, and cron ownership; implementation review cannot determine whether that long-term core product boundary is desired.

options.title: Sponsor the stacked core contract
options.body: Confirm that the read-only planner belongs in core, require the missing inspectable JSON proof, then continue review in dependency order.

options.title: Narrow the surface
options.body: Keep only the smallest diagnostic or planning primitive that maintainers want in core and move the remaining lifecycle workflow to a plugin or future RFC slice.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer this planner until the Claws RFC and its preceding ownership/diagnostics stages have an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the stacked core contract
recommendation.body: Confirm that the read-only planner belongs in core, require the missing inspectable JSON proof, then continue review in dependency order.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned to this PR and authored the concrete review criteria for the planner’s ownership and source-continuity behavior.
